Health & climate Initiative

Reimaging health systems with data and AI

We build data ecosystems and AI-based solutions with research, government, nonprofit, startup and corporate partners, through co-innovation programs.

How can AI help reimaging health systems to prevent the next pandemic or climate-induced health risks?

What key innovations might dramatically improve the healthcare experience for common people, especially in primary care and care continuity?

What data ecosystems do we need to drive such innovations?

What are pragmatic starting points for such a long-term vision?

These questions shape our focus areas and initiatives. To be clear, more than AI, we care about developing AI-based solutions that work, scale, and deliver impact as part of our health systems. Since health systems and AI influence each other’s design, we co-innovate iteratively with system constituents.

We also collaborate extensively with researchers and innovators to tackle critical challenges.

High-Risk Pregnancy Copilot for Frontline Workers

An expert approved, LLM-based assistant that gives instant clinical guidance to ANMs. It is currently deployed and in production with more than 6000 users.

Read more →
AI TRAINER FOR COMMUNITY MENTAL HEALTH

CMHLP’s program to train volunteers in community mental health care has been proven to be effective. Yet training ASHAs at scale is infeasible in an in-person program. ARTPARK and CMHLP partner to develop  multi-agent trainer for ASHAs to make the training process scalable.

Read more →
Kilkari AI Chatbot: Conversational Q&A for Mothers

Our Q&A bot will provide on-demand, real-time, accurate, actionable and personalised information on pregnancy and infant care in an effort to improve health-seeking behaviour that could lead to reduced maternal and child mortality and morbidity.

Read more →
BelonggAI

Billions of people in LMICs with marginalized identities  (gender, caste, disability, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religion) face suboptimal outcomes due to bias and poorly designed programs/policies that ignore their unique needs. These intersectional considerations are often overlooked in SDG activities, leaving gaps in addressing their needs.

BelonggAI and ARTPARK are developing an LLM-based tool to help development practitioners, funders, and researchers uncover and address these exclusions and make their work more inclusive of marginalized groups.
